confidence_notes: The RBA rate is from a search result showing the 18 Nov 2026 observation. I did not open the RBA page itself. Food and drink anchors come from three searches: the RBA rate, a general Chania cost-of-living search, and a cocktail/wine search. Sources disagreed and some were undated, so the figures are rounded aggregates. Beer is about €4.2-4.5 per restaurant serving (aggregates showed €4-4.1, though one regional guide quoted €2.50-3.50). Coffee is about €3.5. An inexpensive meal is about €13. A mid-range dinner for two is about €50-55, in a range of €30-56. Cocktail is about €10, anchored on a crowd-sourced figure of about €9 from only nine data points. Wine by the glass is about €6, since bar menus ranged from €6 to €12. I converted euros to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.15, not a searched rate. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge for peak-season July in a popular Cretan tourist town. I did not search for accommodation or inspect any listings, so they are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Chania is treated as a Greek island tourist city, priced above mainland Greece in July and similar to Heraklion or Rhodes Town in peak season. Prices in the harbour area run higher than in the wider old town.
